root_cause.text: In fastrpc_get_args(), the use of find_vma() instead of vma_lookup() causes an underflow in the DMA offset calculation when the user-provided pointer lies in a gap before the returned VMA, because (ptr & PAGE_MASK) - vma->vm_start becomes negative (unsigned underflow) and corrupts the DMA address.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description states that "find_vma() returns the first VMA with vm_end > addr, but does not check if addr is within that VMA. When the address falls in a gap before the returned VMA, (ptr & PAGE_MASK) - vma->vm_start underflows, corrupting the DMA address sent to the DSP." The patch replaces find_vma() with vma_lookup(), which returns NULL when the address is not contained in any VMA.

When the address falls in a gap before the returned VMA, (ptr & PAGE_MASK) - vma->vm_start underflows, corrupting the DMA address sent to the DSP." The patch replaces find_vma() with vma_lookup(), which returns NULL when the address is not contained in any VMA.

candidates.rationale: Using find_vma() instead of vma_lookup() returns the first VMA with vm_start > ptr, not necessarily containing ptr. This allows the caller to use a VMA that does not cover the address, leading to underflow in the offset calculation.
The check only verifies that a VMA exists, not that it covers the address. This is insufficient because if the VMA starts after the pointer, the calculation will underflow.

This partial statement begins the offset calculation. The (ptr & PAGE_MASK) part gives the page-aligned address of ptr, which may be less than vma->vm_start, causing a negative value when vma->vm_start is subtracted.
This completes the subtraction. Since ptr is before the VMA, subtracting vma->vm_start yields a negative value (unsigned underflow), corrupting the DMA address.

This sets the base DMA address before the vulnerable offset addition. While not directly the cause, it is part of the vulnerable calculation because the underflowed offset is added to this base, resulting in a corrupted final address.
Acquiring the lock is necessary but not directly vulnerable. However, it is part of the sequence that leads to the vulnerable code execution.

vuln_statements.explanation: Using find_vma() returns the first VMA with vm_start > ptr, not necessarily containing ptr. This allows a VMA that does not cover the user address, leading to underflow in the offset calculation when ptr lies before vma->vm_start.

This partial statement computes the offset as (ptr & PAGE_MASK) - vma->vm_start. Since ptr may be less than vma->vm_start, this subtraction yields a negative value (unsigned underflow), corrupting the DMA address.
This completes the offset subtraction. Together with the previous line, the underflowed offset is added to the DMA base address, resulting in a corrupted address.

The check only verifies that a VMA exists, not that it covers the address. This is insufficient because if the VMA starts after the pointer, the offset calculation will underflow and corrupt the DMA address.

This sets the base DMA address before the vulnerable offset addition. While not directly causative, the underflowed offset is added to this base, making the corruption manifest in the final address used for DMA operations.

Acquiring the memory lock is necessary for the VMA lookup but is part of the vulnerable code path. The lock itself is not the cause, but it is part of the sequence that leads to the vulnerable calculation.
